additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

symptom.disease_info: Delusional Disorder is characterized by one or more fixed delusional beliefs lasting at least one month, with overall functioning often relatively preserved outside the area of the belief. It typically presents in mid-to-late adulthood with non-bizarre but firmly held convictions, and is distinguished from schizophrenia by the absence of prominent disorganization, negative symptoms, or broad deterioration in functioning.

patient.stressor_event: Gaining a new family member (e.g., birth, adoption, older adult moving in)
patient.stressor: Allen and his wife agreed to have an older relative move into their home after the relative could no longer manage alone, disrupting the quiet routines of Allen’s workshop, garden, and fishing weekends. Across 9 months, minor misplaced tools, changed schedules, and household disagreements became organized around a fixed belief that the new family member had intentionally infiltrated the home to interfere with his work and property, despite repeated contrary explanations from his wife and neighbors. The belief became the central issue in the household, straining the marriage and leading Allen to make major changes to how he stored equipment and interacted with family. He was brought to psychiatric attention after a family meeting with their pastor and primary care physician made clear that the conviction was not easing and was placing the household under serious strain.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me—my tools don’t move themselves, my fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every weekend, and after all these months I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out.

add_requirements.Functioning is not markedly impaired apa: I still get up, go to the plant, do my assembler work, keep the bills paid, and take care of myself like I always have. The trouble is all centered on what’s happening in my house with him and my things.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve stopped leaving my equipment where I used to, spend a lot of time locking things up and checking the workshop, and I avoid being around him at home. It’s made things tense with my wife, but I’m still managing work and daily responsibilities.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about nine months, ever since my wife’s relative moved into our home.
